producer_brief.topic_summary: Why Ophiocordyceps unilateralis forces a carpenter ant to clamp a leaf vein ~25 cm above the forest floor at solar noon — hijacking muscle fibers directly without melting the brain.
producer_brief.core_dramatic_question: How does a blind fungus steer an ant to an exact microclimate altitude and lock its mandibles even after death?
producer_brief.target_emotion_arc: Uncanny botanical beauty -> eerie realization of bodily puppetry -> quiet natural-history awe.
producer_brief.audience_takeaway: Fungal hyphal networks wrap directly around mandibular muscle fibers, bypassing the ant's central brain like an external puppeteer.

observed_evidence: Infected Camponotus leonardi ants descend from the canopy to bite major leaf veins roughly 25 cm above humid forest soil, predominantly around solar noon.
3D electron-microscopy reconstructions (Hughes / Fredericksen et al.) show dense fungal networks surrounding muscle fibers while leaving the brain anatomically intact.
scientific_inferences: Bioactive fungal metabolites contract mandibular closer muscles into irreversible lockjaw atrophy so the cadaver stays anchored for weeks.
illustrative_abstractions: Translucent cuticle peel showing white-gold hyphal web around muscle bundles vs untouched central ganglion.

anti_clone_declaration.why_not_previous_template: Zero HUD, zero laboratory room, zero cyan/gold telemetry: shot 100% as BBC Planet Earth II / Lubezki sunlit translucent rainforest macro.

beats.narrative_claim: Upside-down under a rainforest leaf, a dead carpenter ant hangs solely by jaws sunk deep into the central vein.
beats.audience_emotion: Uncanny fascination — why didn't gravity drop it?
beats.audience_knows_vs_hidden: Viewer sees locked mandibles piercing leaf tissue; internal fungal puppeteer is hidden beneath black chitin.

beats.narrative_claim: Every victim stops within a razor-thin ~25 cm humidity layer above the mossy floor where spores thrive.
beats.audience_emotion: Chilling precision — realizing a non-random geometric pattern.
beats.audience_knows_vs_hidden: Viewer sees the forest floor height relationship, wondering how the brain was programmed.

beats.narrative_claim: Inside the head capsule, the brain sits untouched — instead, fungal hyphae weave a physical cage directly around jaw muscle fibers.
beats.audience_emotion: Body-horror scientific revelation — trapped inside one's own hijacked muscles.
beats.audience_knows_vs_hidden: Cuticle peel reveals the exact peripheral-muscle hijack mechanism.

beats.narrative_claim: A crimson-tipped stroma erupts behind the head, raining spores straight onto the ant trail directly below.
beats.audience_knows_vs_hidden: Full ecological trap completed across vertical forest space.

beats.narrative_claim: In the quiet emerald understory, the leaf sways once in humid breeze — anchored by jaws that never let go.
beats.audience_knows_vs_hidden: Returns to the mandible clamp now understood as a fungal anchor.
